items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: I worked with Jack Douglas on an Aerosmith record, I got to work with Dave Thoner, with Don Was — like one of the first records was Was (Not Was). And so I got to work on the mix with that

ctx.x: Whatever, we probably weren’t even sure what that meant except that we would have a record. And it seems like most musicians are always trying to get to the next level. And when I hear your story, you went to the next level, but maybe it wasn’t what you thought it would be. But it ended up —

Yeah, you just keep following the way to go. And I mean I went from working at Record Plant and assisting on records. I worked with Jack Douglas on an Aerosmith record, I got to work with Dave Thoner, with Don Was — like one of the first records was Was (Not Was). And so I got to work on the mix with that, and just see how it’s done, and everybody’s sitting there on the console for the mix, just moving faders, doing that. So I learned a lot from a lot of different people who were all at the top of their game, not…

met Charlie Morrow, was one of the clients at Record Plant, and he had like an event business and he also did jingles. He was kind of on the fringe of the jingle industry. And one day we were just talking about synthesis and the future of how that’s going, and that and computer music, and where that is all going to, and he said, “oh I’ve got this jingle project, do you want to work on it with me?” And it was like kind of just doing a video version of the sounder for 10-10 WINS. But it was fun. And then he said,…
